procedural_matters: The panel of the International Jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
facts: In the last minute before the start of Gold Fleet Race 9: GRE 218105 became overlapped from astern close to leeward of UKR 217791.

There were boats close to windward of UKR 217791 GRE 218105 then luffed towards head to wind, UKR 217791 responded by luffing There was contact between the port side of UKR 217791 and the starboard side of GRE 218105 The boats separated.
GRE 218105 then began sculling forcefully, turning down to close-hauled.
The end of GRE 218105’s tiller was outside the boat’s gunwhale.
There was contact between the bow of UKR 217791 and the tiller of GRE 218105 about 30 cm from the end.
The tiller of GRE 218105 broke in two There are scratches on the port side of UKR 217791 GRE 218105 retired.
The tiller was bought second hand but nearly new, and has been used by GRE 218105 for a month.
conclusions: UKR 217791 to windward failed to keep clear of GRE 218105 to leeward, and broke RRS 11. When changing course, GRE 218105 the right-of-way boat failed to give UKR room to keep clear, and broke RRS 16.1 UKR 217791 did not avoid contact with GRE 218105 even though it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a). GRE 218105 did not avoid contact with UKR 217791 even though it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a). GRE 218105, by retiring, took an applicable penalty.
decision: UKR 217791 DSQ race 9. Since GRE 218105 took an applicable penalty, she is not further penalized under RRS 60.5(c)(2).
